text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context; given the infant's age, the seasonal worsening, and your family history of psoriasis, could you show me or describe exactly where on the scalp and forehead the rash is located and how thick the scales appear? REQUEST IMAGES: Scalp_Forehead_Rash.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cradle Cap (Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis).

The combination of greasy yellow scales, erythematous patches on the scalp and forehead of an infant, worsening in cold weather, and a family history of seborrheic dermatitis/psoriasis is highly characteristic of this condition. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Scaling_Sampling. REQUEST IMAGES: CloseUp_Scales.
